tasks.title: Gmail transport: epoch-window list, page drain, quota-aware backoff

tasks.title: auth/gmail_bootstrap.py: loopback + PKCE sign-in that prints the refresh token

runs.tail:
usage: gmail_bootstrap.py [-h] [--force] [--port PORT] [--no-browser] label

Interactive (browser, loopback + PKCE) sign-in for one Gmail label

positional arguments:
  label         mailbox label, letters/digits only, e.g. personal; becomes
                GMAIL_<LABEL>_REFRESH_TOKEN

options:
  -h, --help    show this help message and exit
  --force       mint a new token even if the configured one is healthy
  --port PORT   loopback port to listen on (default: random free port)
  --no-browser  print the URL instead of opening a browser

tasks.notes: Research §1. Desktop OAuth client, auth-code + PKCE (S256), redirect http://127.0.0.1:<random port>, access_type=offline, prompt=consent, scope=GMAIL_SCOPE only. Stdlib http.server + secrets/hashlib + requests: NO google-auth-oauthlib dependency. Validate the state param; exchange the code (send client_secret); refuse to continue if the response has no refresh_token or the granted 'scope' lacks gmail.readonly; print the GMAIL_<LABEL>_REFRESH_TOKEN=... line for the user to paste into .env (never write it to a file). Short-circuit like m365_bootstrap.py: if a token is already configured and check_gmail is ok and not --force, exit 0. Support --port N and --no-browser (print the URL) so the loopback port can be SSH-forwarded from a headless box; that is an implementation note, not a documented Google recipe. Warn that every bootstrap run mints a token and Google keeps only 100 per client (oldest silently invalidated), so do not re-run casually. Unit-test the pure helpers (PKCE pair, URL builder, state check, scope assertion); the browser flow itself is a manual step.

tasks.title: Harden sanitize_text: strip other URI schemes and protocol-relative links
tasks.notes: Found in T-013 review. sanitize_text (pipeline/triage.py, _URL) strips only http(s):// and www. forms; a hostile or confused model reply can still carry ftp://, mailto:, javascript:, data:, file:, tel: URIs or protocol-relative //host/path into the digest, which is later rendered to PDF. Extend the URL removal to those schemes (case-insensitive, also when written with odd spacing is NOT required) and to //host/path forms, removing them the same way existing URLs are removed. Do NOT strip bare domains (evil.example.net, Acme.com): false positives on company names and file names outweigh the gain for a PDF digest; say so in a comment. Keep the existing behavior for markdown links (label kept, target dropped). Add tests to tests/test_triage.py for each new scheme (in plain text and as a markdown link target), for //host, for a bare domain being left alone, and for a sentence where removal leaves no double spaces. The existing 62 triage tests and the injection suite must keep passing unchanged.

tasks.title: Isolate per-message failures in collect_gmail and harden charset decoding
tasks.notes: check finding P1 x2, both reproduced 2026-09-21. (1) _decode_part catches only LookupError around raw.decode(charset, errors='replace'), but a sender-controlled Content-Type charset of 'undefined' raises UnicodeError('undefined encoding') and 'idna' raises UnicodeError('Unsupported error handling replace'); catch (LookupError, UnicodeError) and fall back to utf-8 with errors='replace'. (2) collect_gmail calls flatten_message(msg) with no guard, so ONE message that makes it raise (bad charset, a 2000-deep MIME tree -> RecursionError) discards every already-fetched message and no CollectionResult is returned; the runner then counts a hard failure and after MAX_STUCK_RUNS=3 advances the watermark, losing the window. Wrap the per-message flatten in try/except Exception (RecursionError is an Exception), skip that message, count it as a FAILURE (not the 'unplaceable' bucket) with the message id and exception class in the failure list so the result is 'partial' with the first failure named and every other message kept. Tests: charset=undefined and charset=idna decode without raising; a batch of [good, bad, good] returns both good items with status partial; a 1500-deep nested multipart message (build it programmatically) does not escape; the failure detail names the exception class but never the body.

tasks.title: Bound the cost of HTML-to-text extraction on hostile input
tasks.notes: check finding P2, reproduced 2026-09-21. _TextExtractor.handle_endtag scans the whole open-element stack for every end tag, so unmatched end tags over a deep stack are O(n^2): _html_to_text(''*n + ''*n) took 0.15s at n=2500, 0.56s at 5000, 2.16s at 10000 (30 KB), ~9s at 140 KB, minutes at ~1 MB; the HTML path is reached whenever text/plain is empty, which the sender controls, and nothing bounds the input before parsing (BODY_CAP only slices AFTER). Fix both: (a) truncate the HTML input to a documented MAX_HTML_CHARS (start at 500000, a guess to be re-tuned from the dry run) before parsing, and (b) make the unmatched-end-tag check O(1) (e.g. a collections.Counter of currently open tag names) instead of scanning the stack. Keep hidden-content semantics identical: every existing hidden-content and nesting test must pass unchanged. Tests: the 10000-pair unmatched case completes in well under a second (assert on a generous bound, e.g. < 1.0s, not on exact time), an input over MAX_HTML_CHARS is cut and still yields the visible text before the cut, and a deep but well-formed nest still strips hidden regions correctly.

tasks.title: Give the OAuth loopback listener a real per-connection timeout
tasks.notes: check finding P2, reproduced 2026-09-21: wait_for_code(0, 'S', 1) followed by an idle socket.create_connection to the bound port is still blocked 4s after its 1s deadline. HTTPServer is single-threaded and the handler has no socket timeout, so any local process (or a browser speculative preconnect accepted before the real callback) stalls the accept loop and the real callback waits behind it; the deadline is never enforced. Fix: set a short per-connection timeout on accepted sockets (StreamRequestHandler.timeout, a few seconds) AND enforce the overall deadline in the serve loop (server.timeout + a monotonic deadline check), so the function raises its existing timeout error at the deadline even with a stalled connection open. Also add the loopback-bind test the patterns lens noted is missing: assert the listener's bound address is 127.0.0.1 (server.server_address[0]), not merely reachable there. Tests: an idle connection does not prevent the real callback from being served or the timeout from firing within a bounded slack; a stalled connection followed by a valid callback still returns the code.

tasks.title: Charset hardening: accept only real text codecs and scrub surrogates from decoded bodies
tasks.notes: check finding 1 (P1), reproduced 2026-09-21 by the main thread. _decode_part honors any sender-chosen Content-Type charset that Python knows, including codecs that are not text charsets: unicode_escape, raw_unicode_escape and utf-7 all decode 'hi \ud800 x' (or +2AA-) to a body containing a LONE SURROGATE (U+D800). The collector persists it fine (json.dumps escapes it) but the triage request builder later json.dumps(ensure_ascii=False) then the SDK encodes UTF-8 and raises UnicodeEncodeError. Fix in _decode_part: (a) allow only real text charsets: reject any codec that is not a text encoding (use codecs.lookup(name)._is_text_encoding, and/or an explicit denylist covering unicode_escape, raw_unicode_escape, utf-7, idna, punycode, rot13, base64 and the other bytes-to-bytes/str-to-str codecs) and fall back to utf-8 errors='replace' exactly as for an unknown charset; (b) after ANY decode, scrub lone surrogates (e.g. text.encode('utf-8','replace').decode('utf-8')) so no code path can leave one in bodyText. Also apply the scrub to the header values flatten_message copies (subject, from, to, cc, snippet, messageId, listUnsubscribe) because a JSON header could carry a lone surrogate escape. Keep charset=utf-8, iso-8859-1, windows-1252, shift_jis, gb18030 and utf-16 decoding correct. Tests: each of the three charsets with a surrogate-producing body yields a body with no surrogate; a real windows-1252 and a shift_jis body still decode to the right text; a header value containing a lone surrogate comes out clean; assert on the OUTPUT of flatten_message (no character in 0xD800-0xDFFF in any string field). The existing charset tests must keep passing unchanged.

tasks.title: triage_items: degrade ANY failed call to stubs, never raise
tasks.notes: check finding 1 (P1), second half. triage_items promises never to raise, but its per-call guard catches only (anthropic.APIError, pydantic.ValidationError) at pipeline/triage.py:402. The critic's held-out check showed ValueError, TypeError, KeyError, RuntimeError, RecursionError and UnicodeEncodeError all ESCAPE, so one unexpected failure (for example a lone surrogate reaching the SDK's UTF-8 encode) stops the whole map stage and every item in the window. Fix: catch Exception around the per-call work (the request build, the client call and the response handling), stub that whole batch, and record a failure line with the exception CLASS NAME only (never the message, which can echo email content). Keep a genuine programming error visible in tests by NOT swallowing BaseException (KeyboardInterrupt/SystemExit must still propagate). Update the docstring that currently says programming errors propagate: state the new contract precisely. The retry-then-stub logic for missing aliases must keep working unchanged. Tests (tests/test_triage_client.py, extend only): a client raising each of ValueError, TypeError, KeyError, RuntimeError, RecursionError and UnicodeEncodeError yields every input item as a stub with failures[] naming the class and no raise; KeyboardInterrupt still propagates; ALSO an end-to-end test with the REAL anthropic.Anthropic client (dummy key, max_retries=0) and an item whose body_text contains a lone surrogate: triage_items returns stubs and does not raise (this fails before the fix; the SDK encodes before any network call).

tasks.title: OAuth bootstrap: robust token-exchange errors; pin that the auth code is never logged
tasks.notes: check findings 4 and 6. (a) exchange_code calls body.get(...) on a NON-200 response before checking that the JSON body is a dict: a JSON array or scalar body raises AttributeError, not the TokenExchangeError its docstring promises, and main() catches only BootstrapError so the user gets a raw traceback. Fix: parse defensively (non-dict or non-JSON body -> a TokenExchangeError that names the HTTP status only, never echoing the body, which could contain secrets). (b) Handler.log_message deliberately returns without printing because the default logs the request line, which carries ?code=; the mutant that prints it survives all tests. Add a test that serves a real callback with a recognizable code through wait_for_code under capsys and asserts the code string appears in neither stdout nor stderr. Tests: a 400 response with a JSON array body, a JSON string body, a non-JSON body and an empty body each raise TokenExchangeError (a BootstrapError subclass) with no code, secret or refresh token in the message; the log-suppression test. Existing 24 tests unchanged.
